title: ERP against the finance ledger, October 2026 net revenue
subtitle: Where the ERP and the ledger part, row by row, and how much of the gap each cause accounts for.

verdict.text: EUR 1,471.00 of the EUR 1,506.00 gap is accounted for by named differences and EUR 35.00 on 3 orders is left unexplained, while 8 one-sided rows inside the accounted part (+412.60 ERP only, −150.00 ledger only) still need a reason before the close.

stats.label: One-sided rows, no reason shown
stats.note: +412.60 in the ERP only, −150.00 in the ledger only

items: ERP net revenue (A)
A, definition
Sum of `net_amount` where `status = completed` and `order_date` is in October 2026 (`mart_net_revenue`). `order_date` is the UTC date of `order_ts` on all 1,807 rows.
A, rows and keys
878 rows, 878 order keys, key unique. 38 October rows of other statuses are filtered out.
A, reproduced
Yes, to the cent: the question states EUR 85,390.00.
Ledger amount (B)
B, definition
Sum of `amount` where the date of `posted_at` is in October 2026. One account (`4000-SALES`), one currency (EUR), no filter.
B, rows and keys
862 rows, 858 order keys: 4 orders appear twice.
B, reproduced
Computed from the rows only. The question says the ledger "shows less" and gives no ledger figure, so there is no stated number to check it against.
The gap, A minus B

blocks.title: What I assumed
items: October is 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31 on each side's own date column and clock.
The ledger figure is every row of `ledger.csv` posted in October, because the question names no filter and the file holds one account and one currency.
`order_id` joins the two files. `ledger.csv` carries it for every row.
`posted_at` has no time zone in the file. I read it as local time from how it sits against `order_ts`, see the clock row below.
The ledger extract stops at its last posting, 6 November 2026. Anything posted later cannot be seen here.
Differences of up to 0.50 count as rounding, because every ledger amount is a whole euro.

sections.title: What each difference is
sections.intro: [high] means the rows show it, [med] means the rows point to it, [guess] means no row shows it.

rows: Timing. Orders placed 28 to 30 October that the ledger posted 4.7 to 7.9 days later, on 3 to 6 November, so the ledger counts them in November.

[high] All 7 are in the ledger, in batches 20261103 to 20261106, and all are `standard` line. Every other order with a ledger row (1,710 rows) posts at the order time plus only the clock offset. 89 of the 96 non-staff completed orders of 28 to 30 October posted on time.
Each side follows its own date rule: the ERP by order date, the ledger by posting date. Nothing here says which rule the close should use.
Filter. The finance definition has no staff exclusion, so the ERP figure counts them. The ledger never receives them.

[high] 13 of 13 staff orders in the extract, all completed, have no ledger row, in either month. [med] The BI dashboard leaves staff out on purpose (`revenue_dashboard.sql`), so the exclusion is known practice. No file says whether staff orders are net revenue.
Nothing here can say. By its wording `mart_net_revenue` includes them, and the ledger and the BI dashboard do not.
Clock at the month edges (`time_zone_a` +431.20, 5 orders; `time_zone_b` −318.00, 4 orders), net +113.20
Clock. The same order is dated by two clocks: `order_date` is UTC and `posted_at` is local, so orders in the last hour or two of a month land in different months.

[high] `posted_at` is exactly 2 hours after `order_ts` on orders before 25 October and exactly 1 hour after from 25 October, the date summer time ended. [high] 5 orders of 31 October at 23:03 to 23:59 UTC posted on 1 November, and 4 orders of 30 September at 22:11 to 22:51 UTC posted on 1 October. [med] The ledger clock is CET/CEST; no file names it.
Nothing here can say. No file states which clock the close uses.
In the ERP, not in the ledger (`only_in_a`), +412.60, 6 orders
Real difference. Completed orders with no ledger row up to the last posting in the extract, 6 November.

[high] Only 6 of 1,719 non-staff completed orders in the file have no ledger row, all placed 2 to 15 October, 4 `web` and 2 `store`. [high] All 6 are `value` line with 3 or 4 units, yet 195 of the 201 October orders with that shape posted, so it is not a filter. [med] They are unlikely to be late: the longest posting delay is 7.9 days and they are 22 to 35 days before the last posting.
Nothing here can say. The rows show the ERP has them as completed and the ledger has nothing; no row says why.
Real difference. A second ledger row for an order already posted, inside October, so the ledger counts these 4 orders twice.

[high] 4 orders, 2 ledger rows each, same `posted_at` to the second, same amount, same batch, consecutive `ledger_id`. The ERP has each order once. One pair each in four separate daily batches (3, 5, 8 and 31 October, of 25 to 31 rows), so not a whole batch rerun.
The rows say the ledger is overstated by 268.00: one ERP order, two identical postings. [high]
In the ledger, no ERP order (`only_in_b`), −150.00, 2 rows
Real difference. Ledger rows with no order behind them.

[high] 100.00 and 50.00, posted at 10:00:00 on 29 October and 11:30:00 on 30 October, in ordinary daily batches, with `MAN`-prefixed keys where every other row uses the `SO-` prefix. [med] They look like manual journal entries. No file describes them.
Nothing here can say. The entries' author or backup would.
Unexplained. Same order, same period, the ledger lower than the ERP by 10.00, 20.00 and 5.00.
[high] All 3 are `web`, `premium`, 1 unit, shipping fee 0.00. `order_promotions.csv` has no row for any of them. See the next section.
Rounding. The ledger stores whole euros and the ERP stores cents; the per-row differences net to −4.50.
[high] Every ledger amount is a whole euro. Matched orders differ by at most 0.50.
Neither: it follows from the ledger's whole-euro amounts.

blocks.title: September, same method
blocks.text: September's gap is EUR 824.00 and it splits into staff orders +500.00, the month-edge clock +318.00 and rounding +6.00, adding up exactly. [high] So staff orders, the clock and rounding recur every month. The late postings, ERP-only orders, manual rows, double postings and amount differences appear only in October.

**EUR 35.00 on 3 orders.** Same key on both sides, and the amounts differ by more than rounding. Nothing in these files says why. A manual credit or a discount applied on one side would explain it [guess], and the credit note or the source document of these 3 postings would settle it.

blocks.title: The 3 orders (no keys shown; find them by date and amount)
Placed, but with no reason in the data
blocks.text: These rows are in the buckets above and are counted in the explained total, because they are one-sided rows. Their reason is not shown by any row, and a close should not treat them as settled. The reason would come from the ERP-to-ledger interface log for the 6 orders and from the journal backup for the 2 ledger rows.
